content: === Introduction ===

The liver plays the major role in producing proteins that are secreted into the blood, including major plasma proteins, factors in hemostasis and fibrinolysis, carrier proteins, hormones, prohormones and apolipoprotein:
=== Major plasma proteins ===
All plasma proteins except Gamma-globulins are synthesised in the liver.[1]
<info> Human serum albumin, osmolyte and carrier protein
<info> α-fetoprotein, the fetal counterpart of serum albumin
<info> Soluble plasma fibronectin, forming a blood clot that stops bleeding
<info> C-reactive protein, opsonin on microbes,[2] acute phase protein
=== Factors in hemostasis and fibrinolysis ===

<info> Stimulators of coagulation:
All factors in the coagulation cascade.[3]
While the endothelium does produce some factor VIII, the majority of factor VIII is produced in the liver.[4]

<info> Inhibitors of coagulation: Inactivate an enormous variety of proteinases
α2-macroglobulin
α1-antitrypsin
Antithrombin III
Protein S
Protein C

<info> Fibrinolysis: Breakdown of fibrin clots
Plasminogen

<info> Inhibitors of fibrinolysis
α2-antiplasmin
<info> Complement components C1-9, complement component 3 (C3)
<info> All factors in the coagulation cascade.[3]
<info> While the endothelium does produce some factor VIII, the majority of factor VIII is produced in the liver.[4]
=== Carrier proteins ===
<info> Albumin, carries thyroid hormones and other hormones, particularly fat soluble ones,  fatty acids to the liver, unconjugated bilirubin, many drugs and Ca2+
<info> Transcortin, carries cortisol, aldosterone and progesterone
<info> Haptoglobin, carries free hemoglobin released from erythrocytes
<info> Hemopexin, carries free heme released from hemoglobin
<info> IGF binding protein, carries insulin-like growth factor 1
<info> Major urinary proteins, carries pheromones in rodents
<info> Retinol binding protein, carries retinol
<info> Sex hormone-binding globulin, carries sex hormones, specifically testosterone and estradiol
<info> Thyroxine-binding globulin, carries the thyroid hormones thyroxine (T4) and 3,5,3’-triiodothyronine (T3)
<info> Transthyretin, carries the thyroid hormone thyroxine (T4)
<info> Transferrin, carries iron ions in the ferric form (Fe3+)
<info> Vitamin D-binding protein, carries vitamin D
=== Hormones ===
<info> FGF21, a protein hormone that induces mitochondrial oxidation of fatty acids, hepatic gluconeogenesis, and ketogenesis in response to fasting.
<info> Hepcidin, a peptide hormone that regulates iron homeostasis.
<info> Insulin-like growth factor 1, a polypeptide protein hormone which plays an important role in childhood growth and continues to have anabolic effects in adults
<info> Thrombopoietin, a glycoprotein hormone that regulates the production of platelets by the bone marrow
=== Prohormones ===
<info> Angiotensinogen, when converted to angiotensin causes vasoconstriction and release of aldosterone, in effect increasing blood pressure
=== Apolipoproteins ===
<info> Almost all apolipoprotein, except apo B48 (produced by intestine)
